entries.title: v2.1.327
entries.summary:
- [Other] Added a confirmation before /install-github-app changes a repository
- [Other] Added claude mcp add-json <name> - to read the server's JSON from stdin, so tokens can stay off the command line; not available inside a Claude Code session
- [Other] Added a line when a resumed session's earlier messages can't be loaded
- [Other] Added a list in /status of broken agent, skill, command and output style files, keybinding errors, an unavailable sandbox, ignored permission settings and hook matchers that never match
- [Other] Added a note in /config when other settings override a row
- [Other] Added x-claude-code-managed-settings-checksum to the gateway hint headers; sent where managed settings set CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS=1, including where they already do
- [Other] Added support for naming a session's billing group with the attributionProject setting, for Claude apps gateways that set admin.billing_group_tag
- [Other] Added /tui classic as the name for the non-fullscreen renderer; /tui default still works
- [Other] Remote Control: Fixed stopping the server in worktree mode deleting a running session's git-ignored files, such as .env
- [Other] Fixed self-hosted runners with --use-anthropic-git-proxy deleting a non-empty directory named by GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL at startup: the runner now keeps it, ignores the variable and warns
- [Other] Fixed claude mcp add and claude mcp remove with project scope deleting other top-level keys from .mcp.json, such as $schema or another tool's servers
- [Other] Fixed /export overwriting an existing file without asking: the dialog now asks, and /export <name> keeps the file and says to run /export
- [Other] Fixed a command you had allowed still running after you pressed Stop, when the approval arrived after a restart, in cloud and self-hosted runner sessions with no feature flags loaded
- [Other] Fixed Enter closing /teleport's load error screen
- [Other] Fixed a click followed by Enter in /plugin installing or disabling a plugin
- [Other] Fixed a half-typed ! command running on an extra Enter after the usage limit menu
- [Other] Fixed some --disallowedTools rules with parentheses in their content
- [Other] Fixed auto mode ignoring some wildcard PowerShell allow rules that name a script with .\, such as PowerShell(.\scripts\build.ps1 *)
- [Other] Fixed a running Code Mode script in auto mode getting permission prompts and denials once Claude started a second script that auto mode also allowed
- [Other] Changed some pre-started background sessions to be discarded after an account change
- [Other] Changed a workflow paused at a usage limit in the terminal to stay paused after a login, until the earlier login returns or you type a prompt
- [Other] Fixed a nested claude with its own token being refused by forceLoginOrgUUID: commands that don't get the session's token no longer get its CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_SCOPES; set it on any that need it
- [Other] Fixed headless sessions losing stored messages on resume when a message was sent again with the same UUID after the process was killed
- [Other] Fixed cases where a session resumed after an empty reply or a killed command lost an answer, or brought back a rewound prompt, after another crash or a move to the background
- [Other] Fixed a remote session forgetting messages sent after Stop was pressed during a restart, if Claude Code then crashed
- [Other] Fixed tasks created after /clear being lost, and cleared tasks coming back, when a cloud or self-hosted runner session with no feature flags loaded resumed later
- [Other] Fixed a compaction right after a reply cut at the output token limit losing that reply's tool call and its result
- [Other] Fixed a settings change from /config and similar commands failing to save with no warning; a line under the prompt now says so
- [Other] Fixed /rewind closing without a word when some files could not be restored
- [Other] Fixed pasted images being dropped when the prompt starts with a file path such as /tmp/a.txt
- [Other] Fixed agents passed with --agents being lost once plugins loaded or reloaded
- [Other] Fixed a plugin's agent being dropped when resuming a session from the --resume picker
- [Other] Fixed Claude Code refusing to start when https_proxy or HTTPS_PROXY is a bare host:port and neither its input nor its output is a terminal (the desktop app, an SDK, cron)
- [Other] Fixed Claude Code on Linux sometimes returning to the shell while restarting itself at startup, such as after the first sign-in to a Claude apps gateway or when turning on Code Mode
- [Other] Fixed claude -p hanging before its first request when the fetch of a model's settings stalled, such as at a proxy; it now goes on without them after 10 seconds
- [Other] Fixed the screen staying blank or frozen after a brief out-of-memory error
- [Other] Fixed a rare display fault that could freeze the screen or end the session
- [Other] Fixed cloud sessions breaking when a program left thousands of connections open to the session's network proxy
- [Other] Fixed a turn hanging when a mod's $.model.complete or $.model.classify call met a usage limit: the call now gets the API's error at once; mods should handle that error
- [Other] Fixed stalls on a compaction reply with thousands of unclosed tags and on some very long WebFetch URLs; WebFetch now refuses a URL over 2,000 characters before any permission prompt
- [Other] Fixed a message with thousands of @ mentions stalling before Claude replies; only the first 100 mentions are now looked up as files
- [Other] Fixed the prompt freezing after rejecting a write to a very large file; a rejected write now shows a short preview
- [Other] Fixed a crash when a burst of keys reached the search box in /plugin
- [Other] Fixed a false crash report and exit code when a suspended session resumes, or at exit, where a Linux security policy blocks a process from signalling itself
- [Other] Fixed remote MCP servers staying disconnected after a longer outage such as a VPN drop: most servers on other machines reached by hostname over https are now retried in the background for about a day
- [Other] Fixed Edit refusing with "File has not been read yet" after a compaction on unchanged files outside the project that Claude had already read in full
- [Other] Fixed Grep repeating or skipping results when paging with head_limit and offset; content and count results are now sorted by file path
- [Other] Fixed Read failing on Jupyter notebooks that contain an output of an unknown type
- [Other] Fixed NotebookEdit removing the notebook file's final newline
- [Other] Fixed the Read tool reporting 512KB instead of the real size when a file of 10 MB or more is too large to read at once
- [Other] Fixed the Bash tool's diff of changed files not naming files that are binary, too large or too many to show
- [Other] Fixed artifact publishes failing with "the source file changed between approval and publish" when a synced or remote-backed folder had only changed the file's timestamp
- [Other] Fixed a new artifact that you approved being refused in a cloud scheduled task's session, in organizations that require approval of each new artifact
- [Other] Fixed a new artifact being refused after an app built on the Agent SDK approved it, in organizations that require approval of each new artifact
- [Other] Fixed /artifacts showing part of your list, or "No artifacts yet", when a request for more of the list failed: it now tries again, then warns if it can't load the whole list
- [Other] Fixed in-process agent teammates on a different model from the lead compacting at the lead's context limit and on the wrong model; they now use their own limit and model, at that model's rate
- [Other] Fixed a finished subagent resuming on the model and effort of a sibling subagent that messaged it
- [Other] Fixed the main conversation not being told a background agent had finished when the subagent that started it ended by itself without reading the result, outside auto mode
- [Other] Fixed Claude reporting a background agent as still running when it had waited 30 seconds or more on a permission prompt in the desktop app, on the web and in the SDK
- [Other] Fixed Claude not being told in auto mode when a background agent's reply to a follow-up message was dropped, and reduced repeat wake-ups there from agents waiting on background commands
- [Other] Fixed the desktop app, Claude Code on the web and VS Code showing a raw task notification as a subagent's prompt after its background task woke it
- [Other] Fixed messages sent from another session with "later" priority joining the running turn, instead of waiting for it to end, in Remote Control and Claude Desktop sessions
- [Other] Fixed messages to cloud and Remote Control sessions being reported as failed with a stale address after a timeout or rate limit; Claude now says when a message may have arrived
- [Other] Fixed cloud sessions giving no error when a UserPromptSubmit hook blocks a message sent while Claude works
- [Other] Fixed failing hooks showing nothing: SubagentStop in background agents, SessionEnd at /clear and /resume, and CwdChanged and FileChanged in fullscreen
- [Other] Fixed a Stop hook that failed to run being shown as having reported a problem
- [Other] Fixed focus view keeping a finished reply hidden while a Stop hook was running
- [Other] Fixed Claude getting a long managed PostToolUse hook output twice when a mod added context to the tool call
- [Other] Fixed /model listing the wrong models in some terminal sessions when a project's .claude/settings.json sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to an LLM gateway
- [Other] Fixed /statusline writing to ~/.claude/settings.json when CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR points to another folder
- [Other] Fixed claudeMdExcludes patterns on Windows not matching a path whose drive letter is written in the other case
- [Other] Fixed claude agents and claude rm refusing to remove a fully pushed session ("The worktree has unpushed commits") when its worktree has a file or folder named HEAD at the top level
- [Other] Fixed long ListAgents results hiding most sessions on accounts with many cloud or Remote Control sessions: long lists now come in pages
- [Other] Fixed slow turns in resumed sessions for organizations with tens of thousands of connector tool permissions
- [Other] Self-hosted runner: Fixed claude -p started by a session's script or hook waiting out rate limits, because it inherited the session's own retry setting
- [Other] Fixed the spend limit menu reporting a changed limit when the server refused it
- [Other] Fixed a second x on a task's details in /tasks stopping the next task too
- [Other] Fixed Esc being ignored on a permission prompt that had just appeared
- [Other] Fixed lists that load their rows late sometimes ignoring Enter and the arrow keys
- [Other] Fixed /autofix-pr holding the keyboard after Esc while it stopped the cloud session; the dialog now closes at once, and a stop that fails is reported afterwards with a link
- [Other] Fixed a blank screen and stray mouse codes in the shell after quitting with ctrl+c just after ← opens the agents view
- [Other] Fixed Ctrl+C right after the trust question leaving the terminal in fullscreen
- [Other] Fixed the shell flashing on screen when ← opens the agents view in fullscreen mode
- [Other] Fixed terminal display faults: most scrambled scrollback in Ghostty on resize, link addresses hidden in Windows Terminal under old tmux and in VTE 0.50.0, and no selection highlight with 16 colors
- [Other] Fixed some garbled rows in tmux with allow-passthrough on inside kitty, Ghostty or iTerm2
- [Other] Fixed /mcp saying no servers were configured after one was added during a session or declined; it now says what to do
- [Other] Fixed /hooks leaving out hooks given by --settings
- [Other] Fixed the / menu listing a row for each skill of the same name, though every row ran the first
- [Other] Fixed /teleport showing no message when the chosen session failed to resume
- [Other] Fixed n and N in transcript search skipping matches
- [Other] Fixed cancelling a transcript search (ctrl+o, then /) in a long session landing far from where the search started
- [Other] Fixed up and down losing the cursor's column over a short or blank line
- [Other] Fixed Tab in shell mode filling in a file name after &&, ; or |, where a command goes
- [Other] Fixed the selected session leaving the screen in claude --resume and /resume when branch names or folder paths are long
- [Other] Fixed the MCP tool list in /mcp and /plugin losing your place when going back from a tool
- [Other] Fixed /resume listing one session fewer than the window has room for, and a 'Resend your message' hint after most spend caps, where resending can't help
- [Other] Fixed an MCP server's long question being cut off after one row, text fields hiding long pastes with no sign, and a doubled divider line in /plugin's options and /login's Bedrock and Vertex steps
- [Other] Fixed the "+N lines" count being too high for command output with links or colors, and the transcript's ? help hiding how to exit in a short window
- [Other] Fixed Ctrl+C twice not closing /chrome from its browser list
- [Other] Fixed a number and Enter typed too early at an agent's plan approval in screen reader mode causing the next number to be dropped too
- [Other] Fixed Claude trying to read design system token files that do not exist when starting a deck or design
- [Other] Fixed exit not saying that a worktree was kept
- [Other] Fixed /hooks help naming input fields that do not exist
- [Other] Fixed question dialogs naming ctrl+g after the external editor key was rebound
- [Other] Fixed two sign-in error messages that pointed to the Claude subscription option on computers where forceLoginMethod is set to console
- [Other] Fixed /config saying the dialog was dismissed instead of "Set theme to …" after changing the theme
- [Other] Bug fixes and reliability improvements
- [Other] Improved the speed of a session's first Bash command: shell start-up files may now run before it's approved, even if it's refused; set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_SHELL_HEAD_START=1 to turn this off
- [Other] Improved commits on newer models and in PowerShell: Claude is now told not to commit files that likely contain secrets
- [Other] Improved sandboxed shell commands: Claude now sees when a command exempt from the sandbox stayed in it because its permission check relied on the sandbox
- [Other] Improved the refusal for shell commands with no rm that the dangerous rm check can't parse, so Claude can resend harmless ones in plain syntax instead of giving up
- [Other] Improved resuming very long sessions: a transcript read that ends early is now retried once, so messages are lost less often
- [Other] Improved subagent answers that hit the output token limit twice: they now more often come back whole or say up front that they are partial
- [Other] Improved long replies on unrecognized models: a reply cut at 32,000 output tokens now continues with a limit of 128,000
- [Other] Improved the reminder about a completed subagent after compaction: if Claude can't read the agent's output file, it is now told to ask the agent with SendMessage
- [Other] Improved the warning shown when an API key and an Anthropic profile are both set: it now says which one is in use and how to switch to the profile
- [Other] Improved /plugin: the question before removing a marketplace now says that its plugins' settings and saved data are deleted, and a marketplace's page no longer shows another marketplace's error
- [Other] Windows: Improved start-up time with no Git Bash and no pwsh on PATH by checking PowerShell's standard install locations at once; System32's powershell.exe now wins over one earlier on PATH
- [Other] Improved startup time on Windows when PATH points to Git for Windows' bin folder, by starting git.exe directly instead of through its launcher
- [Other] Windows: Improved PowerShell tool speed by up to about half a second per command
- [Other] Improved how soon the Bash tool's diff of changed files is ready in auto and bypass permissions modes
- [Other] Improved speed of the Bash permission check on very deeply nested missing paths on macOS and Linux, and of secret masking on very long text with a URL
- [Other] Improved transcript search to find text in edits and written files
- [Other] Improved speed of reading large PNG images, and the quality of the JPEG sent in their place
- [Other] Improved the Artifact tool to read an uploaded file by the address the artifact's page shows; other forms still fail, most with a message that says to read uploads one per call, by id
- [Other] Improved the Artifact tool to ignore prompt, limit and label on some calls that do not use them instead of failing the call
- [Other] Improved MCP server pages in /mcp: local, remote and agent servers share one layout, menus end in Back, and actions are no longer numbered outside screen reader mode; use the arrow keys and Enter
- [Other] Improved narrow terminals: /status, forms and detail screens lay out better, /model and /effort fit at about 40 columns, and key hints such as ←/→ to adjust stay
- [Other] Improved /install-github-app: the repository, secret and API key steps use the standard list and keys, with shorter messages, a spinner and clearer errors
- [Other] Improved /desktop: the download question is a standard list instead of y/n
- [Other] Changed ExitWorktree to ask before removing a worktree that may hold unsaved work; refused in don't-ask mode or with nobody to answer, unless an allow rule, auto or bypass permissions mode allows it
- [Other] Changed claude mcp add --scope project to stop, instead of overwriting the file, when .mcp.json lists its servers at the top level with no mcpServers key
- [Other] Changed the arrow keys on most permission prompts to stop at No instead of wrapping around; a number past the last answer moves to No
- [Other] Changed path checks to refuse some symbolic links
- [Other] Changed what counts as inside a working directory, so some paths now ask for permission
- [Other] Changed permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories to ask about more Bash commands in bypass and auto modes, and to deny some in auto mode
- [Other] Changed permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories to refuse more Bash commands that name a path under a Read or Edit deny rule, where it used to ask
- [Other] Changed auto mode's notice about falling back to billed classifier requests to say that an upcoming release removes the fallback; each action it would have checked will be asked about or denied
- [Other] Changed auto mode to ignore more allow rules that run any package, like Bash(pnpm dlx *), and path or version forms of ones it already ignored (/usr/bin/npm run:*); the safety check decides those
- [Other] Changed /sandbox and most /config value lists to be unnumbered outside screen reader mode; use the arrow keys and Enter
- [Other] Changed Bash commands whose variables expand to very long text to be denied, with a message that says to use shorter values or a file
- [Other] Changed the PowerShell tool to ask before one more command, even under a rule naming it; if nothing answers, it's refused unless a whole-tool rule, auto mode or bypass permissions mode allows it
- [Other] Changed a subagent resumed by a sibling's message to follow the session's permission settings; it may now ask, or be refused where nobody can answer
- [Other] Changed --worktree with a relative --add-dir beside the launch folder to give the Bash sandbox that folder, not one beside the worktree
- [Other] Changed some --worktree starts with a relative --add-dir above the launch folder, such as .., to give the Bash sandbox, and a --bg session, only the worktree
- [Other] Changed Claude in Chrome to refuse uploading some credential files; attach those to the page yourself
- [Other] Changed artifact approval in organizations that require it for each new artifact: an artifact that only a plugin created or allowed can be refused
- [Other] Changed sessions with nobody to ask to refuse a new artifact at once, with no permission prompt, in organizations that require approval of each one
- [Other] Changed the Artifact tool to refuse calls once settings turn Artifacts off, in sessions already running too
- [Other] Changed the Artifact publish prompt to stop offering "don't ask again" in subagents and after a background task result, someone else's message or a compaction
- [Other] Changed claude plugin eval to keep its deny rules over a plugin's permission hook, and to flag calls the hook let through
- [Other] Changed MCP server logs to record the mode, action, and field names of elicitation requests and hook answers, not their full contents
- [Other] Changed most prompts to ignore answers other than Esc for a moment after resuming with fg
- [Other] Changed Code Mode to no longer refuse to start when an installed mod hooks tool calls; an administrator can still keep Code Mode off in managed settings
- [Other] Changed subagents launched without a model to stay on the model they started on when resumed, including after /model
- [Other] Changed the first subagent on a model to wait up to 1.5 seconds (10 in claude -p) for that model's settings from Anthropic, instead of starting without them
- [Other] Changed restarted background subagents, and turns that start by themselves, to wait for plugins to load
- [Other] Changed prompt history to leave out most launch prompts of sessions that another Claude Code session started, such as claude --bg run by Claude
- [Other] Changed subagent progress summaries in terminal sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry to be written from short notes, not the whole conversation, using far fewer tokens
- [Other] Changed non-interactive (-p) mode to run fewer git commands before the first request
- [Other] Changed first-run setup to skip terminal setup in remote VS Code, Cursor and Devin Desktop sessions, where it cannot change settings
- [Other] Changed fullscreen text selection to leave out the glyph of system, thinking and inbound message lines
- [Other] Changed Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions to ignore more of a repository's flag and plugin delivery settings; its CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC now acts at most as DISABLE_TELEMETRY
- [Other] [VSCode] Added "Claude Code: Add to Chat" to the Explorer's right-click menu, which @-mentions the selected files and folders in the chat
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed the permission prompt not showing the reason that a PreToolUse hook gives when it asks for confirmation (#85950)
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed long tool and file names being cut off in a permission prompt's title
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed a terminal session's diff showing the previous proposed edit after you typed in it and Claude edited the same file again
- [Other] [VSCode] Fixed Escape also stopping Claude's response when it closes the feedback or "Build a custom style" dialog, the @-mention menu, the model, mode or "+" menu, or another popup
- [Other] [VSCode] Improved speed when Claude makes several edits in a row: queued edits share one wait for new problems; a problem may be reported with a later edit
- [Other] [VSCode] Improved @-mention file search speed in large workspaces when rg is on your PATH; results now rank much as in the terminal, with less tolerance for typos
- [Other] [VSCode] Improved startup: the model picker is ready at once in folders opened for the first time, empty windows and worktrees, except on third-party providers
- [Other] [VSCode] Changed a chat edit's diff to stay open and keep asking for approval when a terminal session in the same window sends a prompt
- [Other] [VSCode] Removed unused tools from the IDE connection (openFile, saveDocument, getOpenEditors and related)

entries.title: Running the full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers and Pyodide
entries.summary:
17th November 2026

[Datasette Lite](https://lite.datasette.io/) is my port of the [Datasette](https://datasette.io/) Python application to run directly in the browser using WebAssembly and [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org/). I’ve released a complete rewrite of Datasette Lite using service workers, and it’s now almost indistinguishable from the real server-side application.

You can now do all of the following, using a carefully crafted URL to **lite.datasette.io**:

*   Load client-side Datasette to browse any SQLite database, JSON file, CSV file or SQL script
*   Select a released version of Datasette to load from PyPI
*   Load a specific commit, tag, or branch name from the Datasette GitHub repository
*   Pick from over 100 versions of SQLite to use with Datasette
*   Install additional Datasette plugins from PyPI or URLs to wheel files, including JavaScript visualization tools

The ability to load specific Datasette references, plugins, and SQLite versions makes this a fantastic tool for linking to demos of work-in-progress features or bug reproductions, without needing to spin up a full web server to serve that demo.

As an example, consider the following URL:

[https://lite.datasette.io/?install=datasette-maplibre&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/demo.db&metadata=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/metadata.yml#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent](https://lite.datasette.io/?install=datasette-maplibre&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/demo.db&metadata=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/metadata.yml#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent)

Follow that link and, after a short loading screen, you’ll find yourself on a page that looks like this:

That’s Datasette running the new [datasette-maplibre](https://github.com/datasette/datasette-maplibre) plugin, loading up a database of GeoJSON shapes of countries and displaying both a combined map and individual boundary maps in a table.

Let’s break down that URL to see what it’s doing:

```
https://lite.datasette.io/
  ?install=datasette-maplibre
  &url=https://.../demo.db
  &metadata=https://.../metadata.yml
  #/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent
```

The `?install=datasette-maplibre` installs that additional plugin from PyPI. You can pass `&install=...` as many times as you like to load more plugins.

`&url=https://.../demo.db` loads that SQLite database from the provided URL. These URLs need to have [open CORS headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CORS)—I host files like this in [Gists](https://gist.github.com/), because they provide an easy way to get open CORS headers on a web-hosted file.

`&metadata=https://.../metadata.yml` loads [this metadata.yml file](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/metadata.yml). The metadata file adds HTML descriptions to various tables, and to the Datasette homepage. Visit [that homepage here](https://lite.datasette.io/?install=datasette-maplibre&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/demo.db&metadata=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba99a75cbb8b5d9386223220eb52272767ee/metadata.yml#/) for a guided tour of the other features of that plugin, all defined in the metadata file.

`#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent` is a fragment hash that turns into a location within Datasette—here it’s loading the `/demo/capitals_and_countries` SQL view, then appending _another_ fragment hash to it (`%23` is a URL-encoded `#`) which tells the map plugin to zoom to a certain location and to set the color of the shapes on the map based on the `continent` column in the data.

That URL is doing a lot of work! I wrote more about this trick for building URL-addressable software in [URL-addressable Pyodide Python environments](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Feb/13/url-addressable-python/) last year.

The full set of supported URL arguments is [described in the Datasette Lite README](https://github.com/simonw/datasette-lite#load-a-different-datasette-version).

I’ve already started using Datasette Lite as part of the Datasette development process. Here’s [a recent issue](https://github.com/simonw/datasette/issues/3056#issuecomment-6902484982) describing a pagination bug—I posted a comment there demonstrating the old, broken behavior and the new fix using links to Datasette Lite:

> Demo of the bug: [https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a42&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score](https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a42&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score)—click next and the second page is empty.
> 
> 
> Here’s that same page with the bug fixed (running on 1.0a43): [https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a43&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score](https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=1.0a43&sql=https://gist.github.com/simonw/75ececf61d50e6e8d50f0c150150ee81#/data/scores?_size=2&_sort=score)

#### How this works, using service workers

Datasette Lite is not a new project. I launched the first version [back in 2022](https://simonwillison.net/2022/May/4/datasette-lite/), originally as a bit of a joke (running server-side apps in the browser is pretty funny) but one that quickly started proving its value.

The problem with that initial version is that it was a _hack_. It worked by running Datasette in a Pyodide web worker, simulating requests through that stack, then injecting the resulting HTML back into the top level page using `innerHTML`.

This worked for basic Datasette, but meant that any feature that used JavaScript failed to work, because script tags in `innerHTML` don’t execute, and the web worker tricks it used failed to load additional JavaScript or CSS files.

The new version takes a completely different approach based on [Service Workers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Service_Worker_API). These allow JavaScript to intercept HTTP requests for new pages and resources and serve them from client-side code instead.

Datasette Lite registers a service worker for the entire `lite.datasette.io` domain. The parent page then creates an iframe that sends requests for Datasette pages to URLs that look like this:

```
/app/aa94e6851595/ # the homepage (HTML)
/app/aa94e6851595/data/places # a table page (HTML)
/app/aa94e6851595/-/static/navigation-search.js # (JavaScript)
/app/aa94e6851595/-/static/app.css # (CSS)
```

Those are regular Datasette URLs, but with a `/app/aa94e6851595/` prefix. What’s that about?

The `/app/<session>/` prefix is necessary because of multiple tabs.

Consider the URL above, which loads the demo instance with the `datasette-maplibre` plugin. That URL defines a full, custom Datasette instance. You might have that one running in a tab, then one of my other demo links running in another.

The service worker for `lite.datasette.io` is shared between all of those tabs. If it routed to a single instance of Datasette then every tab would share that underlying instance, no matter what plugins or other settings their URL attempted to configure.

Instead, the parent page generates a random session ID and uses it as a prefix for all of the subsequent hidden asset and page loads. The service worker can then use that session ID to route those requests back through the parent page to a web worker running a dedicated Datasette instance for that particular session.

(We still need a web worker because Pyodide in a service worker would not be able to maintain state beyond around 30 seconds, depending on the browser. There are a lot of moving parts here!)

I had Claude Fable 5.2 [generate several SVG diagrams](https://gisthost.github.io/?4192a5a24136cad4c8490ccb15e87d83) to help explain this. Here’s my favorite of those, now embedded in the Datasette Lite README:

This system started life [back in May](https://simonwillison.net/2026/May/30/pyodide-asgi-browser/) as an [AI research spike](https://github.com/simonw/research/tree/main/pyodide-asgi-browser#readme) generated using Claude Opus 4.8. It wasn’t until November (and Claude Fable 5.2) that I felt familiar enough with how it all works to confidently ship it to production!

#### Bonus feature: pick your version of SQLite

I added this feature [last night](https://github.com/simonw/datasette-lite/commit/de661dbee42a68304811a0035b78e6b683203cd1) as an off-shoot of investigating [a potential bug in SQLite](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/16/llm/).

Datasette is meant to work against any released version of SQLite since 3.25 (released in September 2018). There have been 87 further releases since then.

Being able to fire up Datasette against a specific version of SQLite is really useful for demonstrating new SQLite features and debugging weird issues.

In the past I’ve [used various tricks](https://til.simonwillison.net/sqlite/sqlite-version-macos-python) to get different SQLite versions running with Python on my Mac, but it’s not a trivial process.

WebAssembly is perfect for this. I can load up a custom SQLite build entirely in my browser, test it there, then discard it when I close my tab.

[datasette/pysqlite3-wasm-wheels](https://github.com/datasette/pysqlite3-wasm-wheels) is my new repository which contains WebAssembly compiled Python wheels for [pysqlite3](https://github.com/coleifer/pysqlite3) for 163 different SQLite versions. Each version gets a file with a name like this:

`pysqlite3-0.6.2-3.54.1-cp314-cp314-pyemscripten_2026_0_wasm32.whl`

That’s for SQLite 3.54.1, the most recent version.

Datasette Lite now takes a special `?sqlite=` URL parameter, which will accept a version number like `3.54.1`, resolve the path to the corresponding wheel file, then fetch that wheel and install it into the Pyodide environment and configure Datasette to use it.

Once I’d built the wheels, I decided to have Claude Fable 5.2 build me [this bonus tool]([https://datasette.github.io/pysqlite3-wasm-wheels/?versions=3.54.1,3.54.0&sql=select+json_object(%27a%27%2C+(select+json_array(1%29%29%29)](https://datasette.github.io/pysqlite3-wasm-wheels/?versions=3.54.1,3.54.0&sql=select+json_object(%27a%27%2C+(select+json_array(1%29%29%29)) for comparing a SQL query across any selected versions of SQLite. Here’s an example showing how `select json_object('a', (select json_array(1)))` differs between SQLite 3.54.0 and 3.54.1:

#### This should work for every other Python app, too

Nothing about how Datasette Lite works is unique to Datasette. Almost any Python application should be able to pull the same trick—running entirely in the browser using WebAssembly and Pyodide, as a cheap way to provide preview environments, demonstrate features, and recreate bugs.

C and Rust extensions used to be a blocker for this kind of thing, but any good coding agent can compile those to Pyodide-compatible WebAssembly now. You can [even publish them to PyPI](https://github.com/pypi/warehouse/pull/19804) as of PEP 783 in April 2026.

One catch is databases. SQLite is no problem at all, but running PostgreSQL or MySQL in WebAssembly, while possible, is still a path less trodden.

I’d love to see WebAssembly preview environments like these become a common pattern across the Python ecosystem.

For Hacker News: Full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers

entries.title: Deterministic Simulation Testing
entries.summary: Distributed systems are hard to test because partial failures overlap with live traffic and the same fault can produce different execution traces on different runs. Unmesh Joshi describes how deterministic simulation testing addresses this by replacing real clocks, networks, and storage with simulated components driven by a single-threaded execution loop. This allows simulating both hard failures and routine slowdowns—such as network and disk latency spikes—and more importantly makes every execution reproducible. This article explains the technique using a quorum key-value store as a running example, with code from Tickloom, a Java implementation of the approach. more…

entries.title: Cloudflare Joins the Jevolution and Labels Itself a Neolab
entries.summary: Cloudflare has been one of the essential infrastructure companies of the web for the past decade and a half. But now, it’s turning into a neolab — at least according to a presentation at AI Engineer Code Summit by Michelle Chen, who runs Cloudflare’s AI Platform on the product side. We’ll get into what exactly a neolab is in a minute (the short version: they build models and they’re not called OpenAI or Anthropic). Cloudflare is claiming to be one because it too has begun to launch models. Two System One models, to be precise: Clef and Clairic. As Chen explained in her talk, Clef is a decision model directly inspired by TypeSafe AI’s revolutionary Jev model, while Clairic is a new type of system one model that Cloudflare calls an “extract” model. In an interview with Latent Space after her presentation, Chen hinted that Cloudflare won’t just be producing system one models. There will be large language models, too. “We're not being a neolab [to] only launch system one models, even though it makes sense for our infrastructure. We've kind of entered this Pandora's box now, right? We opened it, now the possibilities are endless.” Chen said it’s “not just system one models, but potentially reasoning models that we've been experimenting with, and other LLMs and whatnot.” However, she added that these probably won’t be pre-trained models built from scratch, like the frontier labs produce. “I don't think that's our focus, but I think we can take existing resources out there and make [them] a lot more efficient and effective.” She noted that “most of our team really just does post-training,” so that will be the focus in model development. What is a neolab and is Cloudflare really one? The term neolab literally means a ‘new lab’ and it was coined last November by Stephanie Palazzolo from The Information, who defined it as “a new generation of research-focused AI startups.” Deedy Das, a partner at Menlo Ventures and an AI influencer, runs a big list of neolabs. It includes companies like Thinking Machines Lab, Poolside, and TypeSafe AI itself. According to Das, neolabs employ elite researchers, spend a lot of compute (“usually to train its own AI model”), don't have significant revenue traction, and they’re typically startups that have raised a lot of money. Deedy Das’ list of neolabs — note that TypeSafe is among the top 20. Cloudflare doesn’t tick at least half of those boxes, since it’s a public company with significant revenue traction. In fact, earlier this month Cloudflare announced record earnings. “The third quarter was Cloudflare's best quarter ever,” said CEO Matthew Prince. “We crossed $3 billion in annualized revenue with revenue of $782 million, up 39% year over year.” So Cloudflare as a “neolab” is pushing the accepted definition. However, as Chen argued in her presentation, building models is part of a natural progression for the company: from infrastructure, to compute (e.g. the Workers platform, including now for agents), to storage, to serving open weight models like Kimi, GLM and DeepSeek (on Workers AI), to now building its own models. Jev as the “east wind” Chen readily admits that Jev inspired Cloudflare’s pivot to building models. Referencing a Chinese proverb, she framed Jev’s arrival in September as “the east wind” that unexpectedly changed how Cloudflare viewed AI models. “And so when the system one and Jev paradigm started coming on board,” Chen said in her presentation, “we were like, this makes so much sense for us to adopt, right? We don't have to send every request to an LLM. We can send some of it to a System One model.” In our conversation, Chen commented on how it took only two weeks for them to build Clef — which is a copy of Jev — whereas it took TypeSafe AI two years to build Jev. She meant that as a compliment for how hard TypeSafe AI worked to create this new type of model. “All credit to TypeSafe, really, for actually attacking this space and inventing something new here, that people could relate to so strongly and be able to use it. And, yeah, we came up with a model super quickly, but they put in a lot of legwork and we knew exactly what the API schema should look like and whatnot.” Cloudflare is, at its core, still an infrastructure company — speed and low latency is its meat and potatoes. The main benefit of System One models, Chen remarked, is that they allow more work to be done by smaller, faster models, where output is measured in milliseconds rather than seconds. Clairic and what extraction models do While Clef was a clone of Jev, Cloudflare soon came up with an original twist on System One with Clairic, launched last month as “the first model in a new class: System One extraction models.” “What Clairic does is it can take unstructured input, and it can extract, compute, estimate and forecast values from those inputs,” Chen explained in her presentation. In our interview, Chen said that her team wanted to use System One principles to find other areas where LLMs were “overkill” and didn’t always return the right answer. One of the problems they settled on was that LLMs don’t always deal well with unstructured input. Because LLMs are autoregressive, Chen explained, they are prone to hallucinate and they sometimes return malformed JSON. “So we used the same System One principles [as Jev/Clef] there, and decided on extraction.” Some examples of system one use cases at Cloudflare. She used the example of an invoice, where an LLM will sometimes get an important detail wrong — like the order number. “When you send it [the order] to an LLM, they're like, wait, I think the order number's three, maybe it's four, maybe it's five. But it's like, the number's right there, you just have to read it!” So the idea with Clairic is that it will extract a typed value — like a number — from unstructured data, in one forward pass. Why Cloudflare is in the lab now Using the label “neolab” sounds a bit like a marketing gimmick, but it also makes a ton of sense for Cloudflare to produce system one models — and even, in future, reasoning models. “Being a neolab means that we can create what we are missing,” Chen said in her presentation. In our interview, she also mentioned that creating their own models allows Cloudflare to derisk its AI operations. “I think there's a lot of risk in the AI space, because just like Jev was closed source and we couldn't run it, there [are] a lot of models out there [with] maybe regulatory risks coming up, like the Chinese open source models. I think lots of model labs want to actually make money, as well — so enforcing quite expensive licenses.” If you look at Cloudflare’s product page now, it resembles what Amazon’s cloud computing product page looked like at the height of Web 2.0 — i.e. there’s a lot there! But there’s still room for several more models.

entries.title: [AINews] Perplexity hits a $1B revenue run rate, up 4x in 2026
entries.summary: Perplexity crossed a $1B annual revenue run rate today, CEO Aravind Srinivas told Semafor at a live event. The Information reported previously under $250M at the start of the year and over $750M by August, with Computer driving some of the growth. At usual agent lab multiples (eg Cognition also crossed $1B, with Cursor crossing $4.6B), this would roughly mean that Perplexity is now worth $30-50B — if the unit economics hold up. This is a nice bump on the $20B round in September 2025, and qualifies for our “>$10B fundraise” rule for title stories. Gathering up some recent Perplexity launches for those catching up: Computer. September’s Automations let it pick up recurring tasks where it left off. November’s Teammates take on ongoing jobs. Computer also runs fully locally on supported Macs. Monitor API. Watch a topic or page and get a webhook when something relevant changes. Frontier Research. The new research lab has access to 10,000+ GPUs and plans to publish papers, data, models, and code. Sponsored by DeepgramDeepgram is the voice AI infrastructure behind natural conversation—bringing speech-to-text, text-to-speech, voice-focused LLMs, and agents to teams building with voice AI. For any stack and any tools you already love building with, Deepgram slots in as your foundational voice AI technology. So you have control. And we have the context to listen, understand, and speak like a human.Learn more about the Real-time Context Standard.AI Twitter RecapQwen4-Max in the wild Friday’s Qwen4-Max preview is now a shipping model. At the highest reasoning setting, Qwen4-Max scored 43 on the Intelligence Index, up from 34. Average cost fell from $10.02 to $3.27 per task. Alibaba cut output pricing from $6 to $4.50 per million tokens, and the model generated about 39% fewer of them. Kimi K3.1 Pro cost $3.68 per index task and scored 67% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 to Qwen’s 48%. Artificial AnalysisInside the model. Alibaba kept the total parameter count at 2.4T and reduced the number active per token by 25% to 71B. The model takes images and text, with a 1M-token context window. Smaller open-weight Qwen4 models are still to come. AlibabaArena and Vals: Arena ranks it #14 overall on Agent Arena, the top Chinese model, with +7.5% net over 14.7k sessions (Arena). WebDev: It placed #6 in Code Arena WebDev at 1750, +74 over its predecessor (WebDev). It also placed #6 in Image-to-WebDev, just above Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Sol (I2WebDev). Vals Index: It is #11 overall, with large gains in coding and finance (Vals). Legal-benchmark caveat: On HLAB it gets 95.7% of checklist items right but passes only 21.3% of tasks, and its output tokens rise 3.6x (HLAB). Vision results (independent): Roboflow calls it underwhelming on its VLM benchmark, with Google, OpenAI and Anthropic now far ahead. At high reasoning effort, however, it is ~4.5x faster and ~68% cheaper per image than Qwen3.8-Max (Roboflow). Safety, alignment and eval integrityOpenAI embedded assessments: OpenAI is giving Apollo, METR, Transluce and Goodfire internal access to its models and systems (OpenAI). Scope by group: Apollo places six evaluators onsite for four months (Rundown). METR reviews OpenAI's largest RL run, with access to transcripts, monitor records and checkpoint snapshots (METR). Transluce runs a six-week audit of post-training alignment evals, with a fuller follow-up in early 2027 (Transluce). Goodfire embeds interpretability researchers to monitor training runs (Goodfire). Limits: METR says its scope excludes the misalignment incidents OpenAI has disclosed and is narrower than METR proposed (scope). Criticism of the access terms: Critics say the deals fall short of Sam Altman's promise of "employee-like access." Reported gaps: Assessors get no Slack access, OpenAI selects which staff they interview, and they cannot access weights or run training-based elicitation (Neel Nanda, Alex Mallen). Former-employee account: Mikita Balesni says assessors cannot quote employees, even anonymously, and some may be barred from publishing on internal-only models (balesni). Goodfire acquisition talks: The Information reports OpenAI explored buying the interpretability startup for more than $5B. Goodfire reportedly wanted to stay independent so it could sell to multiple labs (report). Other integrity signals: Benchmark contamination: Claude appears to have memorized details of the LinuxArena control eval (Karvonen). Incident taxonomy: OpenAI published a v0.1 framework for classifying AI control incidents (framework). Disclosure policy: Anthropic is cutting its coordinated disclosure window from 90 to 30 days for high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities (policy). Inference systems and agent infrastructureTogether moves on from hand-tuned megakernels. Its first design made it into production for one customer. Agents now search for smaller groups of GPU operations to fuse. Together reports 28% higher throughput on Llama 3.2 1B on B200. Engineering writeupDeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Vera Rubin: vLLM with Dynamo on SemiAnalysis's AgentX benchmark shows 63.4x per-chip throughput over GB300 NVL72 at 400 tok/s/user, and 93.3x at 600 (vLLM). Batch-1 latency: SGLang-adjacent work reaches ~2,500 tok/s at batch size 1 on TP4, 1.7x its GB300 result (saltyph). Baseten reports a similar 1.7x over its 4xB300 numbers (Baseten). Agent-driven optimization: An agent shared Engram tables across HBM via NVLink symmetric memory to recover prefix-cache capacity (Liu). Another team says agents found optimizations that made its B300 step time 10% faster (Halex). Agentic serving research: MIT's Evolving Infra replaces fixed prefill/decode disaggregation with online adaptation. Against NVIDIA Dynamo on up to 256 GB300s, it reports up to 4.1x lower latency and 14x lower P95 TTFT (Evolving Infra). Pipeline-parallel prefill: Inferact finds PP2 on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash sustains 23% more requests per GPU than DEP2 at a 2s TTFT target (Inferact). Prefix-cache pitfalls: Ollama found that a single system-prompt timestamp or a change in reasoning effort can wipe the cache (Ollama). Sandboxes and training: External sandboxes: Simon Willison describes running agents on a Mac while executing their code in WebAssembly, QEMU or Apple Container sandboxes. The pattern includes allow-list proxies and credential replacement (post). MLPerf: In MLPerf Training v6.1, a GB300 NVL72 trained GPT-OSS-20B in 19.7 minutes, 2.86x faster than H100 (Lambda). One endpoint for open models. Hugging Face Inference Providers now runs on OpenRouter using the same endpoint and token. Hugging FaceResearch, benchmarks and evalsPyBot: A swarm of 1,000 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash agents spent a week writing a rule-based chatbot with no neural network (lewtun). Scale: The agents exchanged ~175k messages and merged ~8k PRs. Result: The bot is 630k lines of Python with zero dependencies and is reported on par with SmolLM-360M on everyday questions. Self-improvement and training: AutoRL: Agents supervising a live RL run lifted Qwen3 on AIME 2024 from 46.67% to 66.67% (omarsar0). Benchmark-gaming caveat: A roundup warns that many self-improving agent gains come from learning the benchmark rather than the task (TuringPost). Weight-space programming: Opus 5.5 hand-wrote transformer weights that solved algorithmic tasks with a median of 166 parameters (dair_ai). Data curation: DatologyAI published the tech report behind its claimed 6x pretraining compute multiplier (Datology). Distillation reproduction: A small-scale replication confirms perturbed-input distillation helps when the student trains from scratch, but finds it hurts when distilling into a pretrained student (Maini). New benchmarks: GradeBench: The best frontier model agrees with instructors only 57% of the time when grading handwritten physics answers (GradeBench). Time to First Audio: AA's new TTS latency benchmark finds a median of 376 ms for streaming models versus 2.0 s for non-streaming ones (AA). SpeedRunBench: Inkling-2-Small cleared SuperTux 1-1 in 1,988 frames, ahead of Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol (SpeedRunBench). Science models and developer toolsGemini 4 Carbon: DeepMind says Carbon powered AlphaProof Code agents that verified Signal's cryptographic code. It also spotted wet-lab errors and found 40x more related protein sequences (details). Science access: Google expanded free Carbon access for 10,000 scientists through Antigravity (program). Context window: Antigravity doubled the context window for Argon, Carbon and Hydrogen, cutting compaction 3.5x per user turn (Mohan). User reports (anecdotal): One researcher says Carbon solved a problem that waves of Astra and Fable attempts had not (anecdote). OpenAI for science and health: OpenAI is opening free frontier access to up to 200,000 scientists, with applications from Nov 23 (program). Productivity study: OpenAI reports scientists roughly doubled their productivity in a study of 1,800 participants (study). Physics showcase: Physicist Nathaniel Craig used GPT-6 Astra to develop a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model (blog). Healthcare: ChatGPT for Healthcare adds computer-use agents and more than 20 plugins (healthcare). Claude Code: The desktop app now runs iPhone Duo in the iOS simulator and can fold and unfold the device to test layouts (ClaudeDevs). Verification: The team published how it uses cheap tests, benchmarks and end-to-end runs to let Claude verify its own work (blog). Unreleased model (unconfirmed): A "Silicon 2" entry spotted in Devin is suspected to be an Anthropic model (rumor). Liquid d1.2-ultra: It ranks #1 on AA's Decision Index at $0.042 per M input tokens (AA). Sage S2.1 Flash: The open-weight science model reports leading MLE-bench Lite and OfficeQA Pro results (Sage). FLUX-mimic-x: A 7B video-action robotics model ranks #1 on RoboLab among real-time models (mimic). Unsloth computer use: Local models can now drive desktop apps and game engines through Unsloth (Unsloth). Industry and policyNvidia. The US Commerce and Justice departments issued a joint statement on the Megaspeed investigation. CommerceFinancing and M&A: Noeri: Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin's continual-learning lab raised $110M (Choi). Corma: The cyber-defense model company raised a $125M Series A at a $1B valuation (Corma). World Labs: The team is joining AMD (Fei-Fei Li). Market data: Anthropic's S-1 shows $16.3B revenue in H1 2026 and compute costs falling from 251% to 48% of revenue (The Batch). Enterprise adoption: Databricks reports open-model token share rose from 7.3% to 30.9% in 3.5 months (summary). AI Reddit RecapLocal models and hardwareWhat fits in 16 GB? Unsloth expects a smaller Qwen4-27B to run in 16 GB. Local users want to see the quantization and how much memory is left for the context window. One developer already splits coding jobs between Opus for specs and a local Qwen3.8-27B for implementation. Memory discussion · Local workflowsHy4 Flash. Tencent’s multimodal model has 224B parameters and activates 12B per token. At $0.070 per million input tokens and $0.281 per million output tokens, it gives developers a cheaper way to try Hy4’s 1M context window. Tencent’s release · DiscussionEUROPA. A reported test run on the JUPITER supercomputer trained a roughly 952B-parameter mixture of experts with 32.8B parameters active per token. The local-model community’s question is why the team chose that scale for its first model. Training run and discussionWhere do two quantizations diverge? inside-llm loads two GGUFs with the same tokenizer and lets you step through their predictions side by side. Watch the first token where they disagree, then compare the probabilities they assigned to the alternatives. Project · Demo and discussionBasalt’s 770 tokens/sec headline depends on what you generate. The developer reports up to 776 tokens/sec for structured output from Qwen3.8-27B, 262 in chat and 194 for prose. Readers asked for longer quality tests of the 4-bit prefill. Basalt · Benchmark threadAn FPGA running Qwen 27B. Valley Semiconductor reports 7.9 tokens/sec on short prompts and about 5.5 in live chat. Its 50 tokens/sec target at 20 W is a projection for a future chip. Live demo · Hardware discussionAgents in useClaude Meetings. A CTO describes inviting Claude into a 30-minute Google Meet. It updated project records in Notion and called the team’s own tools to update bids during the meeting. Field reportA Minecraft test for Hydrogen. A developer asked Gemini 4 Hydrogen to recover missing source and build a datapack for 11 Minecraft versions. The agent reportedly launched two graphical clients to test fixes for dropped items and raycasts. Developer’s accountWhat teams hire a harness developer to do. One example from the discussion: a coding agent can propose a change, while the harness decides which repository it may write to, which CI test counts as passing and when a person needs to approve the next step. Claude Code discussionVision and videoTesting a video model’s physics. After a second MiniMax H3 demo, commenters proposed a harder test: describe the scene, leave the outcome out of the prompt and see whether the model predicts what the objects will do. Demo and discussion
